{{Nihongo|'''Akiko Yoshida'''|吉田亜紀子|Yoshida Akiko|born July 22, 1976}}<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kokia.com/blog/50/ | title=冬の苗場にGo！！ | work='Otonami' Music Translator Kokia's Blog | language=ja | date=March 1, 2007 | access-date=March 27, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071124075006/http://www.kokia.com/blog/50/ | archive-date=November 24, 2007 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://big5.chinabroadcast.cn/gate/big5/gb.cri.cn/9964/2006/09/13/1525@1215474.htm | script-title=zh:牛奶@咖啡"山東月"首站人氣高 遇瘋狂歌迷 | publisher=China Broadcast | language=zh | date=September 13, 2006 | access-date=March 18, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727190927/http://big5.chinabroadcast.cn/gate/big5/gb.cri.cn/9964/2006/09/13/1525@1215474.htm | archive-date=July 27, 2011 | url-status=dead }}</ref> is a Japanese singer and songwriter performing under the stage name '''Kokia''' (styled '''KOKIA'''). Her most well known songs are {{Nihongo|"Arigatō..."|ありがとう...|Thank You}} (which reached number 2 in Hong Kong when it was covered by [[Sammi Cheng]]) and "[[The Power of Smile/Remember the Kiss|The Power of Smile]]" (which topped at No. 8 in the singles chart).
She is also recognized for her numerous contributions to [[anime]]/game soundtracks, the most notable being "[[Ai no Melody/Chōwa Oto (With Reflection)]]" for the film ''[[Origin: Spirits of the Past]]'', "[[Follow the Nightingale]]" for the game ''[[Tales of Innocence]]'', "[[Tatta Hitotsu no Omoi]]" for the anime ''[[List of Gunslinger Girl episodes#Gunslinger Girl -Il Teatrino-|Gunslinger Girl: Il Teatrino]]'', "[[Dance of the Spirits]]" for the anime [[The Ancient Magus' Bride|''The Ancient Magus' Bride'']] and "For Little Tail" for the game ''[[Tail Concerto]]''.

Kokia often performs in Europe, basing her activities in Paris and releasing music through Wasabi Records, a subsidiary of [[Kazé]].

==Biography==

===Early life, Pony Canyon debut===
Kokia was born in 1976.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kokia.com/20/2030/2_1.html | title=配信シングル３部作＜Life Trilogy〜いのちの３部作〜＞第２章、配信決定！！ | publisher=Kokia Web | language=ja | access-date=March 20, 2010 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091130125132/http://www.kokia.com/20/2030/2_1.html | archive-date=November 30, 2009 }}</ref> She started playing the violin when she was two and a half years old, but preferred the family piano.<ref name="Habataki">{{cite web | url=http://www.habatakifukushi.jp/interview/int04.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050308114819/http://www.habatakifukushi.jp/interview/int04.html | archive-date=March 8, 2005 | script-title=ja:第４回 ＫＯＫＩＡさん | publisher=Shakai Fukushi Hōjin ([[:ja:社会福祉法人|社会福祉法人]]) | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> Often instead of playing with toys, Kokia played with the family piano.<ref name="Livedoor">{{cite web | url=http://music.news.livedoor.com/person/biography?person_code=029865 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110713215527/http://music.news.livedoor.com/person/biography?person_code=029865 | archive-date=July 13, 2011 | title=KOKIA – バイオグラフィ – 音楽 – livedoor ニュース | publisher=Livedoor | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> Kokia remembers putting picture books on the music stand and creating music that represented the scenes.<ref name="Habataki"/>

When Kokia was 10, she went abroad to America with her sister [[Kyoko Yoshida|Kyoko]] to study at the Summer music school (and did so again when she was 14).<ref name="Livedoor"/> In high school, she studied in vocal music<ref name="Kokiaofficial">{{cite web | url=http://www.kokia.com/30/3010/ | script-title=ja:プロフィール | publisher=Kokia Web | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100205081608/http://www.kokia.com/30/3010/ | archive-date=February 5, 2010 }}</ref> and opera, later majoring in opera at the [[Toho Gakuen School of Music]].<ref name="CDJournalProf">{{cite web | url=https://artist.cdjournal.com/a/kokia/110133 | script-title=ja:アーティスト・プローフィル | publisher=CDJournal | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010| title=KOKIA - CDJournal }}</ref><ref name="Jame-private">{{cite web | url=http://www.jame-world.com/us/articles-4694-private-interview-with-kokia.html | title=Private Interview with KOKIA | publisher=JaME World |date=May 20, 2008 | access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref>

While at university, a friend gave a demo tape Kokia had recorded to a record executive.<ref name="Habataki"/> Kokia was then signed to [[Pony Canyon]], and debuted in 1998 while still at university.<ref name="CDJournalProf"/> She created her stage name by reversing the syllables of her birth name, Akiko (something she had done as a game when she was very young).<ref name="Habataki"/> Her first released song, "For Little Tail", was used as the opening theme song for the game [[Tail Concerto]] (although this was released as the secondary track to the "Road to Glory" single album.){{Citation needed|date=March 2023}}

The leading single from the album, {{nihongo|"Arigatō..."|ありがとう...||"Thank You"}}, found success in Hong Kong. It was awarded third in the 1999 Hong Kong International Popular Song Award.<ref name="CDJournalProf"/> Hong Kong entertainer [[Sammi Cheng]] covered the song, and released it as the eponymous track from her album {{Lang|ja-Latn|Arigatou}} in October 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/arigatou/id278579523?ign-mpt=uo%3D4 |title=Arigatou by Sammi Cheng |publisher=iTunes Store |access-date=March 8, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106150648/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/arigatou/id278579523?ign-mpt=uo%3D4 |archive-date=November 6, 2012 }}</ref> The song became a big hit in Hong Kong, reaching to no2 in the pop charts there.<ref name="Livedoor"/>

===Victor Entertainment===
After the release of her debut album, Kokia did not continue to release music with [[Pony Canyon]].<ref name="TsutayaProf">{{cite web | url=http://www.tsutaya.co.jp/artist/00064902.html | title=ＫＯＫＩＡ アーティストページ – TSUTAYA online | publisher=Tsutaya | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010 | archive-date=April 24, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424052937/http://www.tsutaya.co.jp/artist/00064902.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> Her first releases after this were five songs for [[Luna Sea]] vocalist [[Ryuichi Kawamura]]'s production project, ЯKS, in 2000.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.neowing.co.jp/detailview.html?KEY=VICL-60700 | title=<nowiki>[CD] 彼方まで / RKS</nowiki> |work=Neowing | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> The album was released under [[Victor Entertainment]], heralding in Kokia's relationship with the label. In 2001, she re-debuted in proper under Victor, and released three singles.<ref name="CDJournalProf"/>

Kokia continued to have success throughout Asia, with her music used in Asia-wide ad campaigns.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> In 2001, she performed at two high-profile Chinese concerts: an anti-drugs concert to 30,000 people with the so-called [[Cantopop#1990s: Four Heavenly Kings era|Four Heavenly Kings]] of Hong Kong entertainment ([[Jacky Cheung]], [[Andy Lau]], [[Aaron Kwok]] and [[Leon Lai]]),<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/><ref name="Drugabuse">{{cite web | url=http://www.rthk.org.hk/press/chi/20011117_66_3913.html | script-title=zh:年輕偶像參與港台「禁毒滅罪耀北區」音樂會 發揚正義最大信息 呼籲大眾切勿以身試法 | work=RTHK | language=zh | date=November 17, 2001 | access-date=March 8, 2010 | archive-date=September 27, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120927152352/http://www.rthk.org.hk/press/chi/20011117_66_3913.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> and also to over 120,000 people at a 2001 new year's countdown event in [[Taiwan]].<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> In January 2002, Kokia released her second album, ''[[Trip Trip]]'', her first album to be self-produced.

In 2003, however, Kokia first gained public notice. Her single "[[Kawaranai Koto (Since 1976)]]" was used as the drama [[:ja:愛しき者へ|Itoshiki Mono e]]'s theme song,<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> breaking Kokia into the top 50.<ref name="OriRef">{{cite web | title=オリコンランキング情報サービス「you大樹」 | url=https://ranking.oricon.co.jp | work=[[Oricon]] | access-date=March 8, 2010}} (subscription only)</ref> Her biggest hit, however, was "[[The Power of Smile/Remember the Kiss]]". It gained notoriety after being used in a [[Kao Corporation|Kao]] haircare commercial.<ref name="CDJournalProf"/> After which, Kokia was asked to perform on popular music show [[Music Station]].<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> The single broke the top 20 in Japan<ref name="OriRef"/> and was certified gold by the RIAJ.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.riaj.or.jp/data/others/gold/200310.html | script-title=ja:ゴールド等認定作品一覧 2003年10月 |work=RIAJ | language=ja |access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> The resulting album, ''[[Remember Me (Kokia album)|Remember Me]]'', also broke the top 20, and sold over 45,000 copies.<ref name="OriRef"/>

Her Pony Canyon-era songs "I Catch a Cold" and {{nihongo|"Shiroi Yuki"|白い雪||"White Snow"}} were used in the soundtrack for the popular Chinese drama [[At the Dolphin Bay]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.yesasia.com/global/at-the-dolphin-bay-original-soundtrack/1002839469-0-0-0-en/info.html | title=At The Dolphin Bay Original Soundtrack |work=YesAsia |access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref>

Kokia's fourth album ''[[Uta ga Chikara]]'' (released in 2004) also found modest success, selling 20,000 copies.<ref name="OriRef"/> The biggest single from this album, "[[Yume ga Chikara]]", was used as the encouragement song for the Japan team at the [[2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Athens Olympic games]].<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/>

While Kokia has been associated with game/anime music since her debut, it was in 2006 when a theme song of hers became most successful. Her single "[[Ai no Melody/Chōwa Oto (With Reflection)]]" was used as the two theme songs for the anime film [[Origin: Spirits of the Past]], and it reached number 30 on Oricon's single charts.<ref name="OriRef"/>

In February 2006, Kokia released her greatest hits collection, ''[[Pearl: The Best Collection]]'', and a greatest video clips collection, ''[[Jewel: The Best Video Collection]]''.<ref name="JVCdisc">{{cite web | url=https://www.jvcmusic.co.jp/-/Discographylist/A012051.html | title=KOKIA｜ディスコグラフィー｜@Victor Entertainment |work=Victor Entertainment | language=ja |access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> The best collection reached number 19 on the albums charts.<ref name="OriRef"/>

===Anco and Co., France===

From 2006 onwards, Kokia began working in European markets, as well as taking greater control over her musical releases. In January, she held her first European concert in Paris, and performed at the [[Midem]] music industry trade fair.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> ''Pearl'' was released a month earlier than its Japanese release throughout France and Spain.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/>

In June 2006, Kokia decided to set up her own production company separate from Victor Entertainment, called Anco & Co., after desiring more creative control over her works.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> In November, she debuted in France with the anime-based retailer Wasabi Records, releasing her 5th album, ''[[Aigakikoeru: Listen for the Love]]'', there six months before its Japanese release.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kaze.fr/wasabi/index_boutique_fiche_famille.php?f=16a96c4d7bf1f3d9126ba8d7dfa8a573&typeproduit=4 |title=KOKIA – ai ga kikoeru |work=Wasabi Records |language=fr |access-date=March 8, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723153837/http://www.kaze.fr/wasabi/index_boutique_fiche_famille.php?f=16a96c4d7bf1f3d9126ba8d7dfa8a573&typeproduit=4 |archive-date=July 23, 2011 }}</ref>

In November 2007, Kokia had her second successful game/anime tie-up single, with "[[Follow the Nightingale]]". The song, used for the game [[Tales of Innocence]], reached number 30 on Oricon.<ref name="OriRef"/>

Kokia's greater creative control allowed for her music to be released at a much greater pace. In 2008, Kokia released three albums: the neoclassical ''[[The Voice (Kokia album)|The Voice]]'', the Ireland-themed album ''[[Fairy Dance: Kokia Meets Ireland|Fairy Dance]]'' and her first Christmas album ''[[Christmas Gift (album)|Christmas Gift]]''.<ref name="JVCdisc"/> In 2009, Kokia released two albums simultaneously (''[[Kokia Infinity Akiko: Balance]]'' and ''[[Akiko Infinity Kokia: Balance]]'') to celebrate her 10th anniversary.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> She also held her first world tour, with performances in Japan, France, Ireland, [[Poland]], [[Belgium]] and Germany.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/>

For Kokia's 11th album, ''[[Real World (album)|Real World]]'', she travelled to the Tunisian [[Sahara]] desert for inspiration.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://news.livedoor.com/article/detail/4592802/ | title=KOKIA、サハラ砂漠に感謝と感動を学ぶ |work=Barks | language=ja |date=February 7, 2010 |access-date=March 8, 2010}} {{Dead link|date=October 2010|bot=H3llBot}}</ref>

In 2014, she sang at a number of events in collaboration with Billboard Live Japan which lead up to her first performance with a full orchestra in December 2014, where she sang with the Nihon philharmonic orchestra in collaboration with Billboard Japan.<ref name="billboard classics 2014">{{cite web|last1=billboard|first1=billboard|title=KOKIA falling in love with the orchestra|url=http://billboard-cc.com/classics/2014/08/kokia-falling-in-love-with-the-orchestra%E3%80%80report/|website=Billboard-cc.com|publisher=Billboard japan|access-date=October 16, 2015}}</ref>

In 2017, she sang a memorial song at the joint memorial service for the 10th anniversary of the Chūetsu offshore earthquake (hosted by Kashiwazaki City and Kariwa Village).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mainichi.jp/articles/20170717/ddl/k15/040/048000c|title=中越沖地震：１０年 安全なまち願い 柏崎で合同追悼式 ／新潟|access-date=April 18, 2021|archive-date=April 18, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210418011321/https://mainichi.jp/articles/20170717/ddl/k15/040/048000c|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Since 2017, she has been releasing animal-themed albums as part of the [https://tontonton.gift/ ''tontonton'' project], under the Kokia Jirushi.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kokia.com/blog/2017/ton-ton-ton.html|title = Ton ton ton「どうぶつの音楽会」 | otonami Blog}}</ref>

While the concert was canceled due to COVID-19, KOKIA started the live streaming "1 to 1 Live for you" in April 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://realsound.jp/2020/04/post-545896.html|title=KOKIA、生配信ライブ『1 to 1 Live for you』で届けた音楽を通して人とつながるという温かい循環|date=April 29, 2020 }}</ref> This live streaming is often held on the official KOKIA channel on YouTube.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC7Nj69kzQ3ARDEuetOibj6A|title = KOKIA official - YouTube|website = [[YouTube]]}}</ref> In 2020, she started to distribute the singles digitally while using TuneCore, a music digital distribution service.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tunecore.co.jp/artists/KOKIA?artistPagePath=KOKIA&lang=en|title=KOKIA}}</ref> In 2020, she moved to London, England. ==Artistry==

===Voice===
Her voice is often praised by critics, for its clarity of sound, and she is highly rated as a live singer.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://listen.jp/store/diskreview_6117.htm | script-title=ja:新譜レビュー > ＫＯＫＩＡ／歌がチカラ | work=Listen.jp | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081226005801/http://listen.jp/store/diskreview_6117.htm | archive-date=December 26, 2008 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=試聴記コメント／ガイドコメント | url=https://artist.cdjournal.com/d/songbird/3199051558 | work=[[CDJournal]] | access-date=March 9, 2010}}</ref>
In 2004, on the TV show {{Nihongo||題名のない音楽会21|Daimei no Nai Ongaku-kai 21}}, Kokia attempted to break the [[Guinness World Record]] for the longest note held. In her a cappella performance of [['O Sole Mio]], she held a note for 29.5 seconds, but did not break the record.<ref>Daimei no Nai Ongaku-kai 21. [[TV Asahi]]. Tokyo, July 18, 2004. Retrieved 8 March 2010.</ref>

===Song writing===
Since her second album, ''[[Trip Trip]]'', Kokia has written every original song that appears on her albums.<ref name="TsutayaProf"/> Kokia usually writes all the music for the game/anime OSTs songs in which she appears (though this is not a rule, and some songs have been written by others).<ref name="TsutayaProf"/>

Kokia writes the majority of her songs in Japanese, though many are in English or partial English (such as "The Rule of the Universe", "Say Hi!!", and "So Sad So Bad".). She occasionally branches into different languages, such as Italian ("Il Mare dei Suoni", "Insonnia.") and Irish ("Taimse im' chodhadh" and "Siuil a Run" from her Irish-themed album ''[[Fairy Dance: Kokia Meets Ireland|Fairy Dance]]'').

Occasionally in songs, such as {{nihongo|"Chōwa Oto"|調和　ｏｔｏ|Harmony, Sound}} and "[[Follow the Nightingale]]", Kokia writes lyrics in code. For both of these songs, they featured reversed syllables (such as the lyric "nimiunooto denzush", when reversed gives {{nihongo|"Oto no umi ni shizunde"|音の海に 沈んで||"sinking in a sea of sound"}}).<ref name="CDJ">{{cite web | url=https://www.cdjapan.co.jp/jpop/essentials/kokia/index.html | title= KOKIA Special Feature |work=CDJapan |year=2006 |access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> In "Chōwa Oto", Kokia also has a separate code (the numbers 3 25 15 21 23 and 1) which correspond to the letters of the [[English alphabet]] (1=A, 26=Z) to write the song's name in ''[[wāpuro rōmaji]]'' (C Y O U W A).<ref name="CDJ"/>

=== Musical style ===
Kokia’s work has generally been situated within J-pop while drawing on folk and “world/new-age” colors; AllMusic classifies her under Pop/Rock and International with a “Japanese Traditions” style tag.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.allmusic.com/artist/kokia-mn0000457863 |title=Kokia – Songs, Albums, Reviews, Bio & More |website=AllMusic |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref> Trained in classical voice at Toho Gakuen, she often blends choral textures, orchestral accompaniment, and operatic gestures with pop songwriting.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jasrac.or.jp/otobito/interview02/ |title=音人工房 第2回 KOKIA |website=JASRAC |language=ja |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref> In 2008, her album ''The Voice'' (stylised as ''The VOICE'') received Adlib magazine’s Adlib Awards in the Domestic World/New-Age category, underscoring that reception.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kokia.com/profile/ |title=プロフィール｜KOKIA Official Web |website=KOKIA Official Web |publisher=anco&co. |language=ja |access-date=2026-01-11 |quote=アルバム「The VOICE」が、ADLIB主催の「アドリブ・アワード2008」で「国内ワールド／ニュー・エイジ賞」を受賞}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.amazon.co.jp/VOICE-KOKIA/dp/B00120VGQY |title=The VOICE |website=Amazon.co.jp |language=ja |access-date=2026-01-11 |quote=ADLIB AWARDS 2008 国内ワールド/ニュー・エイジ賞受賞}}</ref>

Her interest in Celtic/Irish idioms is heard on the Ireland-recorded album ''Fairy Dance ~KOKIA meets Ireland~'', a collaboration with local musicians that her label described as a “Celtic healing album.”<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jvcmusic.co.jp/-/Discography/A012051/VICL-63036.html |title=Fairy Dance ～KOKIA meets Ireland～ |website=Victor Entertainment |language=ja |date=2008-09-24 |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref> 

Critics have noted how some anime/game themes employ chant-like writing, layered choir and “opera-esque” passages; for example, reviews of “Follow the Nightingale” (''Tales of Innocence'') and “Karma” (''Phantom: Requiem for the Phantom'') highlight these neoclassical/dark-wave-like sonorities.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rpgfan.com/music-review/kokia-follow-the-nightingale-say-goodbye-good-day/ |title=Follow the Nightingale / KOKIA – Music Review |website=RPGFan |date=2008-04-04 |access-date=2026-01-11 |author=Patrick Gann}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.originalsoundversion.com/getting-to-know-vocalist-kokia-outwork-collection-pieces-review/ |title=Getting to Know Vocalist KOKIA: outwork collection “pieces” (review) |website=Original Sound Version |date=2012-03-30 |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://blog.animeinstrumentality.net/soundtrack-reviews/kokia-pieces-review/ |title=KOKIA: ''pieces'' – Review |website=Anime Instrumentality Blog |date=2014-06-04 |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref>

Separate from her originals, Kokia has issued jazz-standard cover sets (''Watching from Above'' in 2016; ''Watching from Above 2'' in 2019, first released digitally in 2023), featuring material such as “Fever,” “Blue Skies,” and “One Note Samba.”<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jvcmusic.co.jp/-/Discography/A012051/VEATP-42065.html |title=Watching from Above |website=Victor Entertainment |language=ja |date=2023-10-18 |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jvcmusic.co.jp/-/Discography/A012051/VEATP-42182.html |title=Watching from Above 2 |website=Victor Entertainment |language=ja |date=2023-11-22 |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.cdjournal.com/i/news/kokia/107369 |title=KOKIA、洋楽カヴァー・アルバム『Watching from Above2』初配信 |website=CDJournal |language=ja |date=2023-11-22 |access-date=2026-01-11}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Violinist [[Kyoko Yoshida]] is Kokia's older sister,{{citation needed|date=March 2010}} and also attended the [[Toho Gakuen School of Music]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kyokoyoshida.com/profile/index.html | title=ヴァイオリニスト 吉田恭子 オフィシャルサイト：Profile | work=Kyoko Yoshida | language=ja | access-date=March 28, 2010 | archive-date=March 5, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120305101732/http://www.kyokoyoshida.com/profile/index.html | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Kokia's grandfather was the manager of a Japanese shipbuilding company.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kokia.com/blog/602006/ |script-title=ja:＋＋＋ お船の歌 ＋＋＋ |work='Otonami' Music Translator Kokia's Blog |language=ja |date=July 10, 2006 |access-date=March 27, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100402101226/http://www.kokia.com/blog/602006/ |archive-date=April 2, 2010 }}</ref> She created a short film, {{nihongo|"Ojii-chan no Tulip"|おじいちゃんのチューリップ||"Granddad's Tulips"}}, and a song ("Grandfather's Ship") in his honour.<ref name="Jame-exclusive">{{cite web | url=http://www.jame-world.com/us/articles-52150-exclusive-interview-and-video-message-from-kokia.html | title=Exclusive Interview and Video Message from KOKIA | publisher=JaME World |date=July 18, 2009 | access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kokia.com/blog/50/ | script-title=ja:おじいちゃんのチューリップ観た？ | work='Otonami' Music Translator Kokia's Blog | language=ja | date=July 2, 2007 | access-date=March 27, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071124075006/http://www.kokia.com/blog/50/ | archive-date=November 24, 2007 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

Kokia was raised as a Christian, and attended Sunday mass from a young age.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kokia.com/blog/602006/ |title=★ HAPPY NIGHT 4 ★ |work='Otonami' Music Translator Kokia's Blog |language=ja |date=June 17, 2006 |access-date=March 27, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100402101226/http://www.kokia.com/blog/602006/ |archive-date=April 2, 2010 }}</ref> She writes many of her songs about God, such as "Why Do I Sing?", "Everlasting", {{nihongo|"Inori ni mo Nita Utsukushii Sekai"|祈りにも似た美しい世界}} and {{nihongo|"Sei Naru Yoru ni"|聖なる夜に||"In the Holy Night"}}.

Kokia has done humanitarian work for various causes. At high school, she was a member of the volunteer committee, and strived to help the disabled, elderly and AIDS victims.<ref name="Habataki"/> She has performed at a concert for drug abuse,<ref name="Drugabuse"/> supported the Japanese [[Social welfare in Japan|Social Welfare]] Organisation (社会福祉法人),<ref name="Habataki"/> and released a special charity single for the victims of the [[2007 Chūetsu offshore earthquake|2007 Niigata earthquake]].<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> Kokia also feels great sympathy for the [[Memorials and services for the September 11 attacks|September 11]] attacks.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> She gave out 10,000 copies of a special EP, ''[[Music Gift]]'', on the streets of New York City in memory of the attacks.<ref name="Kokiaofficial"/> Many of Kokia's songs are messages about humanitarian/environmental causes,<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.ocn.ne.jp/ecoplus/life/interview/001.html | title=第1回 KOKIAさんにん聞くーエコって本当は自分に優しいことかもー | work=OCN | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120224211010/http://www.ocn.ne.jp/ecoplus/life/interview/001.html | archive-date=February 24, 2012 }}</ref> or about ways for people to live their lives better.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cdjournal.com/main/cdjpush/kokia/1000000309 | title=インタビュー：KOKIA、配信限定シングル３部作の第１弾 "いのち"をテーマに歌われる、ポジティヴなメッセージ |work=CDJournal | language=ja |date=August 6, 2009 |access-date=March 8, 2010}}</ref> Kokia primarily makes songs about love and peace.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.viviana.jp/weblog/kokia/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070930150203/http://viviana.jp/weblog/kokia/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=September 30, 2007 | title=Musictranslator | work=Viviana | language=ja | access-date=March 8, 2010 }}</ref>

Kokia is an avid dog lover. Throughout most of the 2000s, she owned four dogs: Donna, Muta, Nero and Titti.<ref name="inunohanashi">{{cite web | url=http://www.kokia.com/blog/40/ | title=BLOG: 犬の話 | work='Otonami' Music Translator Kokia's Blog | language=ja | access-date=March 28, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071124074935/http://www.kokia.com/blog/40/ | archive-date=November 24, 2007 | url-status=dead }}</ref> However, Donna died in February 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.kokia.com/blog/50/ | script-title=ja:春風にのって | work='Otonami' Music Translator Kokia's Blog | language=ja | date=March 20, 2010 | access-date=March 28, 2010 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071124075006/http://www.kokia.com/blog/50/ | archive-date=November 24, 2007 | url-status=dead }}</ref> She has made references to dogs in several of her songs, such as {{nihongo|"Shiroi Inu to Odoru Yoru"|白い犬と踊る夜||"Night Dancing with a White Dog"}}, and in "Say Hi!!", where the lyrics speak of "driving to the beach to play with our Donna."<ref>{{cite web | url=http://music.goo.ne.jp/lyric/LYRUTND49215/index.html | title=Say Hi!! KOKIA 歌詞情報 – goo 音楽 | work=Goo | language=ja | access-date=March 28, 2010 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120229232351/http://music.goo.ne.jp/lyric/LYRUTND49215/index.html | archive-date=February 29, 2012 }}</ref> Many of her blog posts are centred around her dogs, with a special category dedicated to these posts.<ref name="inunohanashi"/>

extract:
Akiko Yoshida (吉田亜紀子, Yoshida Akiko; born July 22, 1976) is a Japanese singer and songwriter performing under the stage name Kokia (styled KOKIA). Her most well known songs are "Arigatō..." (ありがとう..., Thank You) (which reached number 2 in Hong Kong when it was covered by Sammi Cheng) and "The Power of Smile" (which topped at No. 8 in the singles chart).
She is also recognized for her numerous contributions to anime/game soundtracks, the most notable being "Ai no Melody/Chōwa Oto (With Reflection)" for the film Origin: Spirits of the Past, "Follow the Nightingale" for the game Tales of Innocence, "Tatta Hitotsu no Omoi" for the anime Gunslinger Girl: Il Teatrino, "Dance of the Spirits" for the anime The Ancient Magus' Bride and "For Little Tail" for the game Tail Concerto.
Kokia often performs in Europe, basing her activities in Paris and releasing music through Wasabi Records, a subsidiary of Kazé.
